newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares stage late Wall St-led recovery.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares stage late Wall St-led recovery.

text.p: Swedish shares started weak but staged a late recovery on Friday, helped by a jump in telecoms group Ericsson and strong debt markets with volume steady for the quiet holiday season, brokers said.
The general index ended 1.14 percent up at 3,141.83, against a 1.19 percent fall on Thursday. Turnover was 3.5 bln crowns.

Ericsson was ahead for most of the session, rallying around a higher Wall St start to end up 8 1/2 crowns or over two percent at 326. Insurer Skandia rose four crowns to 328.5, notching up a nearly seven percent gain on the week.

"Many believe in restructuring measures like in Electrolux, but I don't think SKF has much to gain there...It seems more like the European business trends are favourable for the company," one broker said.
Electrolux recently announced sweeping restructuring, including lay-offs. Talk of restructuring in the insurance industry also propelled gains in Skandia.
Forestry shares climbed more on price rises and rumours of a continued strike in Canada. Stora rose 2.5 crowns to 132 and SCA gained 4.5 to 175.5.
